text: Booked the CCDV-F exam for December 12. Plan: about two hours a day for the 13 days of the prep course, then practice exams until I score 80% or more consistently.
Messages API: the API is stateless, so every call resends the whole conversation. content is a list of blocks, so find the text block by its type instead of reading content[0].

stop_reason says why a reply ended: end_turn is a normal finish, max_tokens means the answer was cut off, tool_use means Claude is waiting for a tool result. A max_tokens cut-off is still an HTTP 200, so check stop_reason after every call.

Streaming: register the text handler before awaiting finalMessage. Stream when a person is watching the answer and use a plain call for background jobs. Once an SSE stream has started the status is fixed at 200, so errors travel as an error event.

Sampling: the same prompt can give different answers, so test outputs for a property (parses as JSON, names a fruit) rather than an exact string. Few-shot examples steer the format but can pull answers toward the example's own label.

Structured output, prompt-only: asking for JSON in the system prompt mostly works, but code fences and prose sneak in. Check three layers: stop_reason, then JSON.parse in a try/catch, then a Zod safeParse.

Native JSON with output_config.format: the API generates inside the schema, so fences and prose can't appear. The schema root must be an object, and Zod still checks the rules the schema can't enforce, like minimum lengths.

Extended thinking on Haiku 5.5 is adaptive only: budget_tokens returns a 400. Control the depth with output_config.effort. Thinking spends max_tokens first, so a small max_tokens can leave no room for the answer.
Thinking text is omitted by default on Haiku 5.5; set display to summarized to get a summary. Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens, and thinking can't be switched off at effort xhigh or max.

Tool use: Claude never runs my code. It asks with a tool_use block, my code runs the tool and sends back a tool_result. The loop ends when stop_reason is anything but tool_use, and a turn cap stops a confused model from looping forever.

tool_result placement: every tool_use needs its tool_result in the very next user message, all results in one message and before any text. A missing result is a 400, and splitting results across messages discourages parallel tool calls.

Tool descriptions are Claude's main signal for picking a tool: say what it does, when to use it and when not to. A field description with an example value, like keyword e.g. exam, steers what Claude sends.

strict: true guarantees that tool input matches the schema, but strict mode doesn't support minLength or minimum, so length and count rules still belong in code. An empty string is still a valid string.

Parallel tool calls: independent calls can come back in one response. disable_parallel_tool_use forced one call per turn and cost 46% more input tokens on the same task, because every extra turn resends the transcript.

tool_choice: auto lets Claude decide, any forces some tool, tool forces a named one, none forbids tools. A forced tool on Haiku 5.5 skips thinking. Forcing a tool on every turn of an agent loop means the loop can never end.

Tool errors: send them back as a tool_result with is_error true and a readable message instead of crashing. Claude reads the message and explains or recovers. Finding nothing is a normal result, not an error.

Prompt caching: put the stable part first (tools, system, long documents) and mark its end with cache_control. A cache read costs about a tenth of normal input. Any change before the breakpoint invalidates the cache.

Dropped streams: push the assistant turn into history only after finalMessage resolves. If the user presses Stop, the partial turn is never saved, but tool side effects that already ran don't roll back.
Practice exam 1: 64%. Missed questions on context management, tool_choice and prompt caching. Review compaction versus pruning before the next attempt.

MCP: a server exposes tools, resources and prompts over a standard protocol, so any MCP client can use them. Tools are actions the model calls, resources are data the app reads, prompts are templates the user picks.

Quiz weak spots so far: HTTP status versus content checks, import type versus value imports, where to push the assistant turn, and the tool_result placement rule. Reread these before every practice exam.

Context window: every call resends the whole history, so input tokens grow every turn, and tool results are usually the biggest part. Ideas: prune old tool results, compact old turns into a summary, isolate big sub-tasks.
Workflow versus agent: use a fixed workflow when the steps are known in advance (classify, then route) and an agent loop when they aren't. Workflows are cheaper, faster and easier to test.
Subagents: a subagent works in its own fresh context and returns only its final answer, so the main conversation stays small. Same idea as running a big sub-task in a separate call.
Practice exam 2: 72%. Better on tools, still weak on context management and MCP transports. Next: finish the context lab and redo the MCP lesson.

Haiku 5.5 binds each thinking block to everything sent before it: change the system prompt, the tools or earlier messages and send the thinking block back, and the request returns a 400. Keep conversations append-only when thinking is on.

Token counting: client.messages.countTokens takes the same model, system, tools and messages as a real call and returns input_tokens without running the model. Use it before a call to decide whether to compact.
Caching versus pruning: editing an old tool result changes the prompt prefix, so the cache only helps up to the first changed block. Prune in batches rather than on every turn.
Agent memory: stable facts like the exam date or preferences go in a memory file the agent reads at the start, the current task stays in the conversation, and secrets never go into context.
Human in the loop: put an approval step before irreversible actions like deleting or overwriting notes. The agent pauses, shows what it wants to do, and continues only when approved.
Study group on Thursday: compare answers to practice exam 2 and quiz each other on stop_reason values and tool_choice options. Bring the list of weak spots.
